_note: Canada's curation of the merge (pipeline/merge_ca.py; the decisions and their evidence are in docs/sources/review_2026-10-ca.md). Every entry has a reason. rekind: a source record is another kind of thing. join: records of one structure that the matcher kept apart. apart: records that are not one structure and must stay apart. detach: a record an earlier run filed under the wrong station is forgotten, to be joined elsewhere. hide: a station that is not a light (by id, or by record key before it has an id). rename: the station's display name (its id never changes). merge_stations: two existing stations are one light; the retired id stays on disk with merged_into (ids are permanent).

rekind.reason: Lighthouse Friends' page 'Lower Traverse' is about the lightship station on the St. Roch shoals (a vessel from 1831, a pier lighthouse 1904-07, a vessel again from 1921, a buoy by 1940), not a lighthouse.

join.reason: Lighthouse Friends lists Medway Head and Medway Head (1927) as two pages; they are two towers 72 m apart of one light station.
Pointe du Chene Range Front and Rear: one range, 148 m apart. The matcher could not pair them because the front sits in an OpenStreetMap station called 'North Channel'.
Horse Chops: the lost lighthouse (Lighthouse Friends) and the light OpenStreetMap maps 42 m away, same name; the Coast Guard's 'Flat Rock Fog Signal Station' is a different place 65 m on.
St. Shotts: OpenStreetMap's 'St. Shott's Lightstation' and Lighthouse Friends' St. Shotts, 297 m apart; the Coast Guard list and the staffed-lightstation list both name St. Shotts once.
Heath Point (Anticosti): the standing lighthouse and Lighthouse Friends' lost 'Pointe Heath', 70 m apart, are successive towers of one station.
Cap-de-la-Table: Wikidata's item is 1.1 km from the OpenStreetMap node and Lighthouse Friends' position; one lighthouse.
Little Denier Island: Wikidata and the Coast Guard agree, Lighthouse Friends' fix is 1.2 km east; one lighthouse (the conflict stays on the page).
Flint Island (Cape Breton): Wikidata's item is 3.4 km from where OpenStreetMap, the Coast Guard and Lighthouse Friends put the one light.

Belle Isle South End Lower: the heritage designation (with Wikidata) and the Coast Guard / Lighthouse Friends place it 1.2 km apart; the name is unique to this light (the Upper light is separate, at the Coast Guard's position).
Wood Islands Range Front: Lighthouse Friends' front and Wikidata's front are 3 m apart.
Wood Islands Range Rear: Lighthouse Friends' rear and Wikidata's rear are 5 m apart.

Flowers Cove: Wikidata's item (ARLHS CAN657, Coast Guard N213, the same numbers the Lighthouse Directory gives Flowers Cove) is placed at Harbour Point, 340 km away. It belongs with the Flowers Cove light at 51.308 N.
Algernon Rock (Roche à Veillon): Lighthouse Friends' page and Rowlett's entry describe one light.

apart.reason: Red River Range Light and Black Bear Island Light (Manitoba) are separate pages in every source, 40 m apart.
Bustard Rocks (the lighthouse) and Bustard Rocks Range are separate Lighthouse Friends pages, 89 m apart.
The former Northport back range (inactive) is a different tower from the present Northport rear range, 267 m away.
Two OpenStreetMap lights called Lyal Point on Vancouver Island, 2.3 km apart; only one is the Coast Guard's Lyall Point light.
Wikidata's Pictou Island South item has the west end's coordinates; the west-end lighthouse is a different light 1.3 km from the South light.
Pictou Island West (Lighthouse Friends 2029) is not the South light that Wikidata's item describes.
The Coast Guard's A897 is the west-end light, not the South light that Wikidata's item describes.
Rowlett's Pictou Island West End is not the South light that Wikidata's item describes.

detach.reason: Filed by the first build under the Harbour Point station because its coordinates are Harbour Point's; its identifiers (ARLHS CAN657, Coast Guard N213) say Flowers Cove.
OpenStreetMap's 'Pictou Island West End Lighthouse' was filed under Pictou Island South because Wikidata's item for the South light has the west end's coordinates; it starts the west-end station.
Lighthouse Friends' 'Pictou Island West' (destroyed) is the west-end light, not the 1907 South (wharf) light.
The Coast Guard's 'Pictou Island' (A897, H1244) is the light at the west end (Rowlett: Pictou Island West End, A897).
Rowlett's Pictou Island West End (A897, CAN381, Lighthouse Friends 2029) is the west-end light.
Rowlett's 'Roche à Veillon' (Algernon Rock, 1947 tower, destroyed 2014) is Lighthouse Friends' Algernon Rock, 580 m from Pilier-de-Pierre; it was joined to Pilier-de-Pierre by name.

hide.reason: Not an aid to navigation: tagged private, no lights, no list or register carries it, and the Alberta lighthouse lists name only the lake lights at Sylvan Lake, Lake Newell and Pratt's Landing. Unhide if a source shows a lake light here.
A residential community in Country Hills Village, northwest Calgary, named for a lighthouse theme; no aid to navigation (Alberta has no official lights).

A group designation: the Imperial Towers are lighthouses built to one design in the 1850s on Lake Huron and Georgian Bay and designated together. Wikidata's item sits on Point Clark Lighthouse, which has its own station.
A navy dockyard signal tower at Esquimalt (DY118 is a dockyard building number), mistagged as a lighthouse in OpenStreetMap; no list of lights carries it.
A US lightship vessel (LV-76 / WAL-504 'Relief', 1904, decommissioned 1960) that ended as a derelict on the Fraser River; it belongs with the US Pacific lightship vessels, not with Canadian stations.

Wikidata's 'North Head Lighthouse' has the same coordinates as Brigus Lighthouse (2 m apart): the Brigus light stands on North Head.

Wikidata's Cape St. James is 18.8 km out (52.100 N); OpenStreetMap, Lighthouse Friends and the Coast Guard (P770) agree on 51.936 N.
Two OpenStreetMap elements of Lennard Island Light Station 4 m from the station Wikidata and the staffed list hold (Wikidata's own coordinates are 1.1 km out).
One range, listed twice: a Wikidata item for the whole range with OpenStreetMap's two nodes, beside Wikidata's front and rear items.
Wikidata's item for the whole Wrights Range (4 m from the front light) and the front light with all its other sources.
The front light of the Lower Range, held apart from the range station that has the Coast Guard's entries (34 m).
The rear light of the Lower Range, held apart because the Upper and Lower ranges share a base name.
The rear light of the Upper Range (256 m), held apart because the Upper and Lower ranges share a base name.
Lighthouse Friends names it 'Escarpement Bagot (South Point)': Wikidata's 'Phare de Pointe-Sud' is the Bagot Bluff light, 34 m away.
A second Wikidata item at Pointe de la Prairie, 37 m from the light every other source places there; kept as a structure of that station.
OpenStreetMap's 'Quirpon Lighthouse' (20 m away) is the keeper's house of the Cape Bauld light on Quirpon Island, which runs as the Quirpon Lighthouse Inn.

Grant Beach Range (Miramichi, towers of 1903, inactive since 1972): the front and the rear of one range (DESIGN 3.2). Lighthouse Friends' points are 7.8 km apart because the towers were moved to private land (the front by its owners in 1986).

Two Wikidata-era stations for the one Belle Isle South End Lower light: Wikidata's item carries Heritage Lighthouse 14933, the number of the Parks Canada record in the other station, 1.4 km from the Coast Guard's N234. The kept id is in a story batch.

Pictou Island South (the 1907 wharf light, Heritage Lighthouse 14894): Lighthouse Friends 1642, OpenStreetMap's way and Rowlett's entry made a second station 1.3 km from the first, whose pin was Wikidata's point at the island's west end. The storied id keeps the South light; the west-end records are detached to a station of their own.

Sydney Range: the front (Lighthouse Friends 1648, OpenStreetMap, Rowlett's 2010 replica of the 1905 tower at Dixon Point) and the rear (Lighthouse Friends 1649, Rowlett's old and 2024 rears) of one range, 770 m apart (DESIGN 3.2).
Wikidata's 'Sydney front range light' (a replica, 1.8 km from Lighthouse Friends' front) is the same front light; no source has a second Sydney front range.

Wallace Harbour Range (1904): the rear tower was sold in 1994 and moved in 1995 to Malagash Point as a summer home (Lighthouse Friends 1005), 13 km from the front; one range, one station (the storied front's id).
Pelee Passage: the 1902 tower, replaced on the passage in 1975 (Rowlett), now stands at Lakeview Park Marina, Windsor (Lighthouse Friends 1040). One station, its old tower relocated.
Stokes Bay Range: the 1904 rear tower was flown out by helicopter in 2009 when a new rear was built (Lighthouse Friends 1595), so the sources place it 52 km from the front; one range.
Brighton Beach Range: front (storied id) and rear, 400 m apart, with Wikidata's item for the pair (DESIGN 3.2).

Leards Range: the front (Wikidata 'Leards Range Front Lighthouse', Lighthouse Friends 970, Rowlett's Victoria Harbour, OpenStreetMap's 'Victoria Range Light') and the rear (OpenStreetMap's 'Leards Back Range Light', Lighthouse Friends 971, Rowlett's rear, Wikidata's item for the pair), 880 m apart. The kept id is in a story batch.

Malpeque Harbour Approach Range: Lighthouse Friends' rear (937, on Fish Island) is the rear light of the range whose station holds Wikidata's item and the OpenStreetMap rear node, 1 km away; one range.

Malpeque Outer Range (Darnley Point, towers of 1922): two stations 590 m apart hold its two lights; OpenStreetMap and Lighthouse Friends label front and rear the other way round, but they are the two halves of one range.
Miminegash Range: the old wooden rear tower was moved to a private cottage near Kildare (Lighthouse Friends 948), 18 km away; one range.

Northport Range: the 'Former Northport Back Range Light' (1897, moved to private land, Lighthouse Friends 991), Wikidata's item for the range and Lighthouse Friends' and Rowlett's rear are the storied station's range.
Summerside Outer Range: front and rear, 430 m apart, with Wikidata's item for the pair (DESIGN 3.2).

Calvaire (Cap Charles) Range: the 1915 front tower was moved by Deschaillons in the 1980s to a rest area at the village's western entrance (Lighthouse Friends 1478), 3.6 km from the range; one station.
Soulanges Canal Upper Entrance Range (1902-1960): front and rear, 490 m apart (DESIGN 3.2).
L'Ardoise range (Lower L'Ardoise, 1909, inactive about 1970): Lighthouse Friends' front (private, 4.2 km away) and the station holding Wikidata's item and the rear; one range.

Pugwash (Fishing Point): the 1871 tower (Lighthouse Friends 'Pugwash (Old)', destroyed 2018) and the 1962 tower (Wikidata, Lighthouse Friends 'Pugwash', demolished 2023), 1.3 km apart on the same point under one name; successive towers of one station.
Murray Harbour Range: Wikidata's 'Murray Harbour Back Range Light', the Coast Guard's rear (A965) and Rowlett's rear are the rear the storied station already holds through Lighthouse Friends 956.
Cape Tryon: the 1905 tower, retired in 1969 when the present tower was built, was moved to private land 3.9 km away (Lighthouse Friends 'Cape Tryon (Old)'); one station, the storied id.

Cap de Rabast (Pointe-Nord, Anticosti): Wikidata has two items, 'Cap-de-Rabast Lighthouse' (a rounded point) and 'Phare de Pointe-Nord'; OpenStreetMap, Lighthouse Friends, the Coast Guard (A1515.2) and Rowlett all describe one light.

The Coast Guard's 'Flat Rock Fog Signal Station' (N463, Admiralty H522) is 80 m from Horse Chops; OpenStreetMap's Horse Chops element carries H522 and Rowlett gives Horse Chops (fog signal) N463. The fog signal station is a structure of the Horse Chops light station (the first review had left it apart).
Bon-Désir: Wikidata has two items, 'Cap-de-Bon-Désir Lighthouse' (rounded point, 250 m) and 'Phare de Bon-Désir'; Lighthouse Friends, the Coast Guard (A1755) and Rowlett describe one light.
Port Dalhousie Range: Wikidata's 'Outer' and 'Inner' range lighthouses are the front and rear that Lighthouse Friends, OpenStreetMap and Rowlett call Range Front and Rear, 460 m apart; one range.
Summerside Range: Lighthouse Friends' and Rowlett's front (private, inactive) is the front of the range whose rear is Wikidata's 'Summerside Back Range Light' (Coast Guard A1022); one range.
Wikidata's 'Old Lighthouse' at Lakeside Park, Oakville, is the 1889 Oakville harbour lighthouse moved off the pier; one station with the present Oakville light.
